content.text:
Current internal model — what I can report now:

View A: attention is almost certainly on the right location (selection ~0.999). That right object is very likely red and very likely a square. Upper is represented as a yellow circle but is not being attended. Lower appears as a blue triangle; left appears as a green cross. The right location has the highest predicted recoverability now and after one and two steps. If you command a retargeting in A, the model predictably moves attention: an "upper" command will select the upper location, "right" keeps the right, "lower" selects the lower, and "left" selects the left (each with ~99.9% probability). Thus the system can be directed to any of the four A locations.

View B: attention is almost certainly on the lower location (selection ~0.999). That lower object is very likely green and a cross. Right is represented as a blue square; upper is likely a red triangle; left is likely a yellow circle. Recoverability for B's lower location is lower than A's attended item. If you issue directional commands in B, the model will overwhelmingly move selection to the right location (commands upper/right/lower/left all predict selecting right with very high probability).
